answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks when each new identity must bond to an established sponsor whose stake is slashed if the clone ring converges kin-like. Juries rotate peer sets so a single colluding meadow cannot capture consensus, and every clone pays a per-identity deliberation cost: a pre-composed cipher cannot shortcut fresh work, so N clones cost N times one identity's labour. History-weighted standing gives newcomers votes near zero value, so honest agents rise together toward the zenith of reputation.
